statement: Let isUpper(b) mean 65 <= b <= 90. A byte sequence t is a tag name iff 1 <= len(t) <= 9 and for every i with 0 <= i < len(t), isUpper(t[i]). Define valid content and valid closed tag mutually recursively as follows. A byte sequence c is a valid content iff there exist an integer k >= 0 and byte sequences p_1, ..., p_k such that c = p_1 ++ ... ++ p_k (with k = 0 meaning c is empty) and for each i in 1..k, p_i satisfies exactly one of: (a) p_i is a single byte b with b != 60; (b) p_i is a valid closed tag; (c) p_i is of the form `<![CDATA[` ++ d ++ `]]>` where d is any byte sequence that does not contain the contiguous subsequence `]]>` (i.e., there is no j with 0 <= j <= len(d)-3 such that d[j]=93, d[j+1]=93, d[j+2]=62). A byte sequence s is a valid closed tag iff there exist a tag name t and a byte sequence c such that s = `<` ++ t ++ `>` ++ c ++ `</` ++ t ++ `>` and c is a valid content. (Here `<`, `>`, `/`, `!`, `[`, `]` denote the single bytes 60, 62, 47, 33, 91, 93, and the 9-byte string `<![CDATA[` is 60,33,91,67,68,65,84,65,91; the 3-byte string `]]>` is 93,93,62.) Then the function returns a result r and r = true if and only if code is a valid closed tag.
preconditions: code is a byte slice (slice of 8-bit unsigned integers) with 1 <= len(code) <= 500, and every byte of code is one of the following ASCII codes: 97-122 (a-z), 65-90 (A-Z), 48-57 (0-9), 60 ('<'), 62 ('>'), 47 ('/'), 33 ('!'), 91 ('['), 93 (']'), 46 ('.'), or 32 (' ').
